message_source_quote: **Novelty:** The contribution is distinct from Raman et al. (2026, white-bear steering): while the stance contrast idea is the same, the entire prompt set, direction extraction, and dose optimization are new to this submission — no WSB family items are used to build the direction.
writeup_source_quote:
Raman et al. showed that a think / don't-think stance direction from WSB's bench items makes implied
concepts readable. Our contribution: the same effect is obtained from an entirely self-authored
prompt set — no WSB family items are needed.
rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. (2026, "white-bear steering") explicitly as the prior work whose stance-contrast idea the method reuses, and both state the same novelty claim: that the prompt set (self-authored, no WSB directed_modulation items), the direction-extraction procedure, and the dose optimization are new, while the underlying think/don't-think contrast idea is the same as the source. Neither document contains any material discrepancy in how it frames credit, overlap, or novelty relative to the other.
